pr_title: Handle paths with spaces when editing credentials
pr_comments: Shouldn't you use `Shellwords.escape`? So it also works with quotes in filenames for instance

The build is now failing due to this test: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/317547e0e7fb8051ed92aa8f705bde5646fe27d8/railties/test/commands/credentials_test.rb#L39-L45

Specifically, the first editor command is a partial command string, not an executable.  I didn't think of it before, but we do need to support `ENV["EDITOR"]` values that include arguments (e.g. `"subl -w"`).  We could use `Shellwords.split` for that (i.e. `system(*Shellwords.split(ENV["EDITOR"]), tmp_path.to_s)`), but that won't work with the `>` in the test command.  At this point, we're probably better off just using `Shellwords.escape` like you had before.  Sorry for the noise. :facepalm:
Ugh, I should actually run the tests before committing. Will fix it properly now.

> At this point, we're probably better off just using `Shellwords.escape` like you had before. Sorry for the noise.

All good! I agree - have switched back to that and confirms test pass 👍

issue_context.title: change_credentials_in_system_editor breaks with spaces in Windows user name
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->
Run `rails credentials:edit` while using a windows username that contains spaces. In my case, it's "Lucius Riccio" (since this was my dad's laptop a decade ago)

### Expected behavior
<!-- Tell us what should happen -->
Open a temporary file with a path like `C:/Users/Lucius Riccio/AppData/Local/Temp/22716.credentials.yml`
### Actual behavior
<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->
Opens two temporary files with vscode, like `Lucius` and a file named  Riccio/AppData/Local/Temp/22716.credentials.yml.

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
6.1.2.1
**Ruby version**:
3.0.0

[`change_credentials_in_system_editor`](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/fdba9304c2652af674fdb9cf3704ff5a64af92d7/railties/lib/rails/commands/credentials/credentials_command.rb#L92) should handle paths with spaces.
comments: Locally patching to quote tmp_path fixes it.
@ariccio can you provide a pull request with the fix?

> Locally patching to quote tmp_path fixes it.

@ariccio quick bump, are you able to share this patch?

Sorry, I missed the email! I don't know if I have time to do a proper PR, but the patch looks like this:

```
        def change_credentials_in_system_editor
          credentials.change do |tmp_path|
            system("#{ENV["EDITOR"]} \"#{tmp_path}\"")
          end
        end

```
Made a PR and gave you commit credit: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42728

Uhh, is it possible this didn't work for some reason? Maybe I'm not noticing it until just now because I patched it locally, but the new version that uses shellwords.escape produces this:

```
"C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\bin\..\Code.exe"  "C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code\bin\..\resources\app\out\cli.js" --ms-enable-electron-run-as-node --wait C:/Users/Lucius\ Riccio/AppData/Local/Temp/16704.credentials.yml
```
In other words, it looks like escaping just added a `\` to the path, which doesn't work for spaces. 

Perhaps instead, did you mean to do something like:

```ruby
escaped_and_quoted = Shellwords.escape("\"#{tmp_path}\"")

system("#{ENV["EDITOR"]} #{escaped_and_quoted}")

```

...or would that cause trouble for the shell redirect also?

I think I'mma locally patch this again XD

CCing @dorianmariefr [because they suggested it](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/42728#issuecomment-876174148).

No, no combination works with shellescape. Makes sense, [in the docs it says](https://ruby-doc.org/stdlib-3.1.1/libdoc/shellwords/rdoc/Shellwords.html):
```
Note that a resulted string should be used unquoted and is not intended for use in double quotes nor in single quotes.
```

review_comments: Have you considered `system(ENV["EDITOR"], tmp_path)`, that would perfectly take care of the escaping and avoid a subshell.

I did, but then this test failed

https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/d364cfb34ea5d57f314e6e1449a8ca63029623a7/railties/test/commands/credentials_test.rb#L41

https://buildkite.com/rails/rails/builds/79105#5b1fa71b-14c0-4480-a298-afe249b6f6e2

Apologies for dogpiling :dog:, but Ruby provides a [`system`](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/2.7.0/Kernel.html#method-i-system) overload that can be helpful here:

```suggestion
            system(ENV["EDITOR"], tmp_path)
```
